The Old Shells answer three questions in a generation, and nobody can predict which three.
The Veil of Shadows has played the same play every night for about a hundred and forty years.
The Council’s mint has twice bought back the Mint-in-the-Mire’s false Anchors by mistake.
By custom, only Council seats and the Concord’s high clergy wear reefpurple.
A Tarvan horn-bow costs fifty Anchors, and no guild makes it.
Sporrn salve heals in days what takes weeks, and costs three Tides a pot.
Knot-speech, the tongue of the Below, has no names in it at all.
A mirror plover must spend one full year with its person before it speaks.
Vault geese guard the Reckoners’ Hall, and cannot be bribed.
The Pocchin cheat at Nine Ports. Everyone knows, and everyone plays them anyway.
Tidecall has no clock. The match ends when the tide reaches the callstone.
The great match of the year is the Charter Match: the Armada against the Hunters.
Every guest at a Vorthani monastery carries one stone somewhere before leaving. Half the walls were built by strangers.
In Snowvah you pay for your meal before you eat it.
A cat-kin’s byname is the number of lives they have left.
Nobody rides a centaur. The few who were carried were carried once, as a debt.
An ivory-kin carries one memory for the whole herd, and wears it as a name.
The water of the Slowwater rises and falls twice a day, and no tide reaches it.
A patch can’t be bought. A card can. Islanders are very clear on the difference.
A company with a ship takes the ship’s name, and paints its old one small on the stern board.
Proof make carries a guild stamp. Harbor make costs a tenth as much and fails when it matters.
A scribe charges a Bit a page.
Whoever sheltered with you through a Long Night is kin for life.
A cup hung upside down in an island kitchen belongs to someone who is at sea.
The Banestorm brothers share one Ranking card and have asked for two every year.

sections.title: A ship at sea, step by step

blocks.text: *The short version, for players. Each step says where its rules are.*
**Know your ship.** Its stat block gives its Armor Class, Hull Points, Damage Threshold, Speed in battle, travel pace for a day, Seaworthiness, crew, cargo, and guns (Part Two).
**Know your crew.** Green, Able, Blooded, or Veteran. The crew's quality bonus goes on its gun attacks, its seaworthiness checks, and its morale (Part Three).
**Each day at sea,** the GM rolls the weather, the navigator keeps the course or makes a check, a d20 says whether something finds the ship, and everyone aboard eats and drinks (Part One).
**When the weather turns,** the helm makes seaworthiness checks, and anyone on deck in a storm keeps hold of a line (Part One).

**When it comes to a fight,** each of you takes a station: Captain, Helm, Master of Thunder, Chartmaster, Rook, Sword-Warden, Bosun, Ship's Tidecaller, or Oathwarden. The ship moves and fires on its own turn, and you still take yours (Parts Three and Four).
**When one ship runs,** the chase is counted in hours, not rounds. A lead of 5 and the quarry is over the horizon; a lead of 0 and the guns begin (Part Five).
**Afterward,** the crew patches what it can at sea, and a yard mends the rest for about a tenth of the hull's price (Part Four).
The passages everyone knows (What Everyone Knows, §3) are fair passages for an ordinary merchantman, ports and weather included:

rows: Varan Port to the far ice

blocks.text: A fast hull cuts a third off the time.
A convoy adds a third.
Tip to tip, the Frontier to the far ice, is five to six months.
At the table, a ship's **travel pace** (its stat block) is the distance it makes in a full day of fair sailing. Use it for passages off the known routes, and for chases and races that matter.
Each day of a voyage, the GM runs four steps.
**Weather.** Roll on the weather table for the season (below).
**Navigation.** In charted waters, a competent Chartmaster keeps the course without a roll. Off the charts, in fog, or after a storm, the navigator makes the check below.

**Encounters.** Roll a d20. On an 18 or higher, something finds the ship: a sail on the horizon, a sea-beast, wreckage, a storm-front, a stranger in the water. On the King Tide's Three Nights, an encounter comes on a 12 or higher.
**Provisions.** Each person aboard needs a day's food and a gallon of fresh water. A ship that runs short uses the 2024 rules for hunger and thirst.
Roll a d20 each morning and read the column for the season. Fair Water is summer; Storm Water is autumn.
**Becalmed:** a sailing ship makes a quarter of its travel pace. Galleys and the *Iron Swan* do not care.
**Fair:** full travel pace.
**Fresh wind:** a fast hull makes a third more than its travel pace; everyone else makes their pace.

**Gale:** half pace. Each person without Sea Legs (Player's Companion, Part Four) makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or has the Poisoned condition (seasick) until they finish a Long Rest ashore or a calm day passes. The ship makes a DC 10 seaworthiness check (below).

**Storm:** no progress. The ship makes a DC 15 seaworthiness check, and anyone on deck without a line makes a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check each hour or goes over the side.

**Seaworthiness.** The ship's helm rolls a d20 and adds the crew's quality bonus (Part Three) and the ship's Seaworthiness modifier. On a failure the ship takes 4d10 Bludgeoning damage that ignores its Damage Threshold, and the GM picks one: a mast sprung, a boat lost, cargo shifted, a hand overboard.
The navigator makes an Intelligence check with **Navigator's Tools** (or a Wisdom (Survival) check, at Disadvantage, without them).
**DC 10** for coastal waters with landmarks.
**DC 15** for open sea off the charts, in fog, or after a storm.
**DC 20** on the far southern fog-seas, and anywhere near the Wrong Coast.
On a failure the ship loses a day; on a failure by 5 or more it is lost, and does not know it until the next landfall.
Help the navigator with:
A **Chartwright's chart** of the waters: Advantage.
A **landfall petrel** or a **homeward snail** (Beasts and Companions): the petrel finds the nearest land, the snail finds home.
The Sea Legs feat's **Weather Eye**: no roll is needed to read tomorrow's weather.
**Ship's food:** salt-fish, hard biscuit, saltknots, pickets, and whatever was bought in the last port. Fresh water is the true limit of any voyage: an ordinary ship carries water for about a month.
**Watches:** four hours on, four hours off. A character who stands a night watch gets no Long Rest that night unless a lullaby cricket sings (Beasts and Companions).
**Customs:** the first drop of every bottle over the rail; never whistle for wind; a Tide in your boot sailing south; no sailing on a Graveday.
**Companions aboard:** a lampet honks at weather the glass has not caught; a leak rat finds the leak; a knot crab keeps the knots; a tidehound goes over the side after the drowning.

**Size and type:** most ships are Gargantuan vehicles. A ship is an object for the rules: it has no ability scores but Strength and Constitution for checks, and it is immune to Poison and Psychic damage and to every condition.
**Armor Class:** how hard the hull is to hurt.
**Hull Points:** the ship's Hit Points. At half, its Speed is halved. At 0 it is **crippled and sinking** (Part Four).
**Damage Threshold:** damage from a single source below this number does nothing to the hull. Swords and arrows do not sink ships.
**Speed:** how far the ship moves in a round of battle, in feet, with a fair wind.
**Travel pace:** miles in a full day of fair sailing.
**Seaworthiness:** the modifier to the ship's seaworthiness checks.
**Crew:** the fewest hands who can sail it, and a full complement. With fewer than the minimum, the ship can't make way.
**Cargo:** tons it can carry, and passengers beyond the crew.
**Weapons:** its guns, by side, and anything else that bites.
**Price:** new, from a yard (Volume XXI).

rows: Grapeshot: can target crew on a deck instead of the hull (Dexterity save DC 13 in a 15-foot cube, half on a success).
Fires every other round; can't hit a target within 300 feet.
On a hit against a creature, it is tethered to the ship (escape DC 16).
Ignores Damage Threshold. Fires once, then its battery must be recharged (a day in port, and a Krysta charge worth 50 Orsals). Rare and ruinous; the Admiralty owns a handful.

blocks.text: A ship's **battery** is a group of guns that fires together as one attack. A battery uses the ship's crew-quality bonus (Part Three) as well, so the attack bonus above is for an Able crew.
A crew's quality is a single bonus added to its ship's gun attacks, its seaworthiness checks, and its morale.

rows: Grey Coats, pressed men, a merchant's first voyage
Most merchant crews and Armada hands
Armada crews after their first action; most pirate crews
The Killing Tide, the Standing Storm, Free Tide flagships, the *Crimson Tide*

blocks.text: A crew rises one step after a season of hard sailing and a real fight, at the GM's word. It falls one step if it loses a third of its hands.

A merchantman of sixty hands costs about **100 to 120 Anchors a month** in wages (Volume XXI). A deckhand earns about **1 Anchor a month** and found, an able seaman **1½ Anchors** and a share of prizes; the rest goes to the officers.

**Shares:** privateers and pirates sail on shares instead of wages. Under the Free Tide's articles, a hand takes one share, an officer one and a half, the captain two, and the ship's fund takes one in ten before anything is split.
**Signing on:** a crew hired in a strange port is Green until it has sailed a month together.
In a sea-fight, each player character can take a **station**. A station gives that character something to do on the ship's turn, besides their own turn.

rows: **Command:** choose one other station; it gets Advantage on its roll this round. Also makes the crew's morale checks.
A character with Navigator's Tools or Water Vehicles
**Steer:** move the ship, and make the check for a maneuver (Part Four).
**Fire:** each battery that can bear makes one attack. The gunner adds their proficiency bonus to one battery's attack.
**Read the Water:** a DC 15 Intelligence (Navigator's Tools) check; on a success, the ship ignores difficult water (shoals, reefs) this round, or gains a +2 bonus to its next chase roll.
**Spot:** a Wisdom (Perception) check to see what is hidden: a ship in fog, a reef under the swell, a sea-beast rising.
**Marines:** lead the boarding or repel boarders (Part Four).
**Damage Control:** a DC 13 Intelligence check with Carpenter's Tools; on a success the ship regains 2d10 Hull Points, or a fire, a breach, or a fouled rig is cleared.
**Bless the Line:** a DC 13 Wisdom (Religion) check; on a success, the crew has Advantage on its next morale check.
**Hold the Line:** the crew can't strike its colors this round.

blocks.text: A ship with no one at a station still does the basics: an Able crew steers, fires its guns, and patches holes, but only the stations make the rolls that change a fight.
When a ship falls to half its Hull Points, loses its captain, or is boarded by a stronger crew, its crew makes a **morale check**: a d20 plus the crew-quality bonus. On a 10 or higher, it fights on.
On a failure, a merchant crew strikes its colors; a pirate crew tries to run; an Armada crew, sworn to the Charter, fights on but takes Disadvantage on its next attacks.
The Oathwarden's station and the Ship's Tidecaller's blessing exist for exactly this moment.
A sea-fight uses ordinary 6-second rounds, so that characters can fight, cast, and board in the middle of it. Each ship takes a **ship's turn** on its captain's initiative. On the ship's turn:
**Move:** the helm moves the ship up to its Speed. A ship can turn up to 90 degrees once during its move. It can't move backward.
**Stations act:** each station held by a character does its thing, in any order.
**Guns:** each battery that bears fires once. A battery bears on targets on its side of the ship; bow chasers bear ahead.
Characters still take their own turns. A character at a station uses their action on their own turn for anything else they like; the station's work is done on the ship's turn.
At the start of a sea-fight the GM sets the wind's direction.
**Running before the wind:** +10 feet of Speed.
**Across the wind:** normal Speed.
**Into the wind:** half Speed. A sailing ship can't sail straight into the wind at all.
**The weather gauge:** the ship that is upwind chooses the range at the start of each round, unless the other wins a maneuver against it.
When the helm wants more than a plain move, it makes a **maneuver**: a Wisdom check with Navigator's Tools or Water Vehicles, adding the crew-quality bonus. An opposing helm can contest it.
**Hard Over (DC 15):** turn a second time this move.
**Cross the T (contested):** move across the enemy's bow or stern. Until the enemy's next turn, the enemy's broadside can't bear on you, and your batteries have Advantage against it.
**Take the Gauge (contested):** take the upwind position from the enemy.
**Evasive Sailing (DC 13):** until the ship's next turn, attacks against it have Disadvantage, but its own guns have Disadvantage too.
**Come Alongside (contested if the enemy is unwilling):** end your move within 10 feet of the enemy, ready to grapple.
A battery's attack hits if it equals or beats the target's Armor Class. Damage below the target's Damage Threshold does nothing.
On a natural 20, or when a single hit deals three times the target's Damage Threshold or more, roll on the critical table.

rows: **Fire!** The ship takes 11 (2d10) Fire damage at the start of each of its turns until the Bosun puts it out.
**Mast down.** Speed halved until repaired in port.
**Rudder jammed.** The ship can't turn until the Bosun frees it.
**Gun deck smashed.** One battery on the struck side is out of action for the fight.
**Hull breach.** The ship loses 10 Hull Points at the start of each of its turns until the Bosun patches it. A leak rat aboard tells the Bosun exactly where.
**Rigging fouled.** The ship can't move on its next turn.
**Officer down.** A non-player officer of the GM's choice is killed or taken out of the fight. The crew makes a morale check.

**Magazine.** The Bosun makes a DC 15 check at once. On a failure, the powder goes up: the ship takes 55 (10d10) Fire damage, ignoring its Damage Threshold, and everyone aboard makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or takes 22 (4d10) Fire damage.

blocks.text: A ship that moves at least 30 feet in a straight line and ends its move against another ship can ram it. Both ships take Bludgeoning damage: the rammed ship takes 4d10 for every 10 feet of the rammer's Speed, the rammer half that. A ship with a ram (the GM decides who has one) takes none. A ramming ship can come alongside and grapple in the same move.

**Grapple:** two ships within 10 feet can be grappled together by the side that wants it, with a contested Strength check between the two crews (d20 plus crew-quality bonus). Grappled ships can't move until the lines are cut (a crew's action, or a character's Utilize action on each line).

**Boarding:** while ships are grappled, crews can board. Player characters fight the boarding as an ordinary battle at **the point of the boarding**, against the enemy's officers and their best fighters.

**The rest of the deck:** each round, both crews roll a d20, adding their quality bonus and +1 for every full twenty hands they have more than the other side. The loser loses a tenth of its hands. When the player characters win their fight at the point of the boarding, their crew wins the deck. When they lose it, the enemy does.
**Repelling boarders:** the Sword-Warden's station gives the defending crew Advantage on its first deck roll.

At 0 Hull Points a ship is **crippled and sinking**. It can't move or fire. It goes down in 1d6 × 10 rounds, sooner if it is burning. Its crew takes to the boats, strikes its colors, or swims. A sinking ship can be saved only by a Bosun who succeeds on a DC 20 check while the ship is still afloat, which leaves it with 1 Hull Point and dead in the water.
**At sea:** a day of work by a ship's carpenter and crew restores a tenth of the ship's Hull Points, up to half its maximum.
**In port:** a yard restores everything. The cost is about a tenth of the hull's price after a hard fight or a hard storm (Volume XXI), and a week to a month of time.
A chase at sea is measured in hours, not rounds. Use it when one ship flees and another follows, and the gap is more than a gunshot.
**Set the lead.** The quarry starts with a lead of 1 to 3 (the GM decides, from the distance).

**Each hour,** both helms make a **chase roll**: a d20, plus the crew-quality bonus, plus 1 for every 10 feet of Speed the ship has over the slower ship, plus any trait bonus. The Chartmaster's Read the Water adds 2.
**Compare.** If the quarry wins, its lead grows by 1. If the pursuer wins, the lead shrinks by 1. On a tie, roll on the complications table.
**Ends:** at a lead of 5, the quarry is gone over the horizon. At a lead of 0, the pursuer is in gunshot, and the battle round begins.

rows: **Squall.** Both ships make a DC 10 seaworthiness check.
**Shoals.** The quarry may cut across them: a DC 15 helm check to gain 2 lead, or run aground on a failure.
**Fog.** The Rook of each ship makes a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check; a ship that fails loses the other for an hour.
**The wind backs.** The ship with the weather gauge loses it.
**A third sail.** Another ship appears on the horizon. Friend or foe, the GM decides.
**Sprung spar.** The ship that rolled lower loses 10 feet of Speed until repaired.
**Nightfall.** The quarry gains 1 lead, and the chase continues by lantern, or by none.

blocks.text: **Reefs and shoals:** hidden in bad light. The Rook spots them with a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check; a ship that strikes one takes 6d10 Bludgeoning damage that ignores its Damage Threshold and may be holed (a hull breach).

**The Stillwater:** a circle of open sea that no wind crosses. A sailing ship that drifts into it is becalmed until it is rowed or towed out, a day of hard work for every boat it can put in the water. Galleys and the *Iron Swan* cross it as they please.
**Fog-seas of the ice:** the far south's fogs last for days. Every navigation check is at Disadvantage, and every encounter comes out of the fog at close range.
**Sea-ice:** a ship without ice-strakes makes a DC 13 seaworthiness check each day in the pack, or takes 4d10 Bludgeoning damage.

**The Wrong Coast:** the Sealed Waters of the far south, closed by the Council in 148 EC as "plague waters." The Armada turns back any ship it sees going in. Southern sailors tell of grey ships with no names that sail without lanterns, and of **the Hum**, a note under hearing that you feel in the hull on calm nights. *Never hum along.*
For the Three Nights of a King Tide:
Every port closes, and a ship at sea is on its own.
Encounters come on a 12 or higher.
The highest water in three years floats ships over reefs they could never cross, and strands them on islands that are not there the next morning.
What lives in the deep water comes up. The Killing Tide sails on the Three Nights for exactly that reason.

A ship that sails through the waters of a Coral court sails under that court's sea-pact (Bible Lite, §10). Break the pact (poach a reef, foul the water, spill blood in it) and the court may answer with weather, with a lost anchor, or with something that rises.

ships.title: The Armada's classes
ships.intro: Every class has a duty with teeth (Bible Lite, §6). Each is crewed by the Armada's Able or Blooded hands (Part Three), and each carries the special posts aboard: an Oathwarden, a Sword-Warden, a Ship's Tidecaller, a Master of Thunder, a Chartmaster, and the Rook.

fields: 1 battery of light guns per side; two swivel guns
traits: **Dispatch Rider.** A Harbinger gains a +4 bonus to chase rolls.
notes: Courier. “A Harbinger means news, and news is rarely good.”

ships.name: Vindicator (sloop)
fields: 2 batteries of light guns per side; a long gun in the bow (bow chaser)
traits: **Bow Chaser.** It can fire its bow gun at a ship it is chasing, ahead of it.

ships.name: Justicar (river gunboat)
fields: 50 miles on a river, 40 at sea
2 carronades fore and aft, turning to either side; four swivel guns
traits: **Shallow Draft.** It can go where a seagoing ship would run aground.

ships.name: Warden (frigate)
fields: 4 batteries of long guns per side; 4 swivel guns

ships.name: Juggernaut (heavy frigate)
fields: 5 batteries of long guns per side
traits: **Storm-Runner.** It has Advantage on seaworthiness checks, and a gale does not halve its pace.

ships.name: Interdictor (cruiser)
fields: 6 batteries of long guns per side; 2 carronades fore
traits: **Line of Fire.** Once per round, when a ship comes within 600 feet of it, it can fire one battery at that ship as a reaction.
notes: Blockade and area denial; the Iron Blockade’s fist.

ships.name: Dreadnought (ship of the line)
fields: 8 batteries of long guns per side; 4 carronades

ships.name: Enforcer (bombard)
fields: 4 bombard mortars; 2 batteries of light guns per side
traits: **Siege-Ship.** Its mortars deal double damage to buildings and fortifications.
notes: Delivers the Council’s verdict to fortresses.

ships.name: Executioner (man-o-war)
fields: 10 batteries of long guns per side; 6 carronades; some carry a Krysta cannon
20,000 Orsals and a decade of Council argument
traits: **Flag of the Fleet.** Every allied ship within a mile that can see its flag adds 1 to its crew-quality bonus.

ships.title: A ship everyone has heard of

ships.name: The Iron Swan
fields: 40 ft., in any wind or none, and against the tide
90 miles, whatever the weather short of a storm
a crew of living flame; no one has counted them
unknown; ships that have fired on her have not said
traits: **No Sails.** Wind, calm, and gale do not affect its Speed or travel pace.
**Burning Wake.** Water within 30 feet of its hull boils at full steam. A creature that starts its turn in that water takes 11 (2d10) Fire damage.
**Iron.** It is immune to Fire damage, and ramming it is a very poor idea.
notes: The only steamship in the world, captained by Titania, Gold Hunter, eleventh in the Ranking.

ships.title: The Wingates' hulls
ships.intro: The Wingates' Kalvatar branch sails seven ships, tied up at the old dock of the Thorne Estate. Most are brigs built for the Front, and every crew is a veteran one.

ships.name: Wingate War-Brig
fields: 30 to 110 (sailors who fight, and soldiers who sail)
2 batteries of light guns per side; a long gun in the bow; four swivel guns
traits: **Wingate Crew.** Its crew is Veteran (+4), and losing hands never drops it below Blooded. On the rest of the deck it gains +1 for every full ten hands it has more than the other side, not every twenty.
notes: A brig built for the Front, carrying soldiers as much as cargo.

borrow.who: The Council, or one of the Five
A great house, or one of the Twelve Flags
Anyone the Hall will not lend to

insure.voyage: Between the Frontier and the Heartland

wanted.notice: By order of the Council of the Charted Isles. The following captains are wanted for piracy, murder, and crimes against the Charter. Bounties are paid by the Reckoners' Hall on proof, dead or alive, unless marked otherwise. Bring the captain, the ship, or the flag.

captains.name: Seren Blackheart, "the Last Smile"
docks: Her father's ghost guides her in battle.
She knows where the Kraken's Lair lies.
A sea witch's pact gives her unnatural skill.
signs: A pale grinning crescent on a black flag.
A flagship old sailors swear went down at the Kraken's Maw.
Free Tide colors on every hull around her.
deeds: took a Charterhouse Company salt-hulk without firing a shot
sailed into the roads with more ships behind her than the Council admits
let a whole crew go ashore and kept only their ship
sent word that any crew tired of its masters may sail under the crescent

captains.name: Corvath Stormbringer
docks: He cannot die.
His crew are ghosts that steel passes through.
He throws lightning from his own hands.
His ship sails inside a storm that never ends.
signs: A knot of cloud and lightning moving against the wind.
A storm that stood in one place all night and was gone at dawn.
Men at the rail who did not get wet.
deeds: passed a convoy close enough to hail, and took nothing
struck a coaster's mast with lightning and sailed on
was seen standing off a harbor where a ship went down the week before
rode out a gale that sank two honest ships

captains.name: Captain Blackstorm
docks: He commands the dead with whispered words.
He wears the lost Ring of Depths, which gives him power over sea creatures.
He once outmaneuvered the whole Armada during a King Tide.
signs: Old Maw veterans' tattoos on every arm in the boat.
Grey sails on a hull that runs without a wake.
Crews from the Kraken's Maw drinking on his coin.
deeds: fought two of the Last Smile's ships to a standstill
signed on a whole crew of Maw survivors in one night
slipped an Armada patrol in a fog
raised one of Blackheart's old flags beside his own

docks: Her singing voice lures ships onto her guns.
Her crew is all women and has never lost a boarding.
signs: Singing over the water before any sail is seen.
A deep blue hull worked in silver and gold.
A boarding party of women, every one of them armed.

boarded a merchant galley while her crew sang
took a Flag's brig and returned its cook with a letter of thanks
won a boarding in the time it takes to sing a verse

Her crew is bound to her by an unbreakable oath of the sea.
She keeps a hidden cove where runaway slaves are sheltered.
signs: Chains thrown over the side after a boarding.
A red hull off the plantation coast.
A crew that cheers when it takes a slaver.

burned a plantation house's private sloop at its own jetty
landed forty runaways on a coast nobody charts
raised the price on her own head by humiliating a colonial magistrate

captains.name: Siroc the Swift

He carries an ancient elven artifact that commands the winds.
He has escaped the Armada more than a dozen times.

A ship that was there, and then was not.
A wake where there was no wind.

took a strongbox and nothing else
outran a squall into harbor and out again before the bells
left a pursuing captain becalmed with a full wind on his own sails

They stole the Crown of Winter.
signs: Frost on the rigging of ships in warm water.
A brother and a sister at the helm, together.
Plunder sold at Varan Port before the news arrives.

were seen far north of any ice, with ice around them

rates_en: **An iron** fetches top coin, because it carries no name and cannot be traced: 150 to 300 Anchors in the season before the Trials. That is the whole trouble with irons.
**Smuggler's freight** is double honest freight; dark glass and guns go at triple.
**Laundering** coin through the Sunspine Run's betting-books costs a fifth, paid to the Crest Syndicate.
**Company brass** is bought from the Company's workers at half its face, and sold back to the Company's clerks at three-quarters. Everyone knows exactly what is happening.
rates_es: **Un hierro** se paga a precio alto, porque no lleva nombre y no se puede rastrear: de 150 a 300 Anclas en la temporada antes de las Pruebas. Ese es todo el problema de los hierros.
**El flete de contrabandista** es el doble del flete honrado; el vidrio oscuro y las armas van al triple.
**Lavar** dinero en los libros de apuestas de la Carrera del Espinazo del Sol cuesta una quinta parte, que se le paga al Sindicato de la Cresta.

**El latón de la Compañía** se les compra a los trabajadores de la Compañía a la mitad de su valor, y se les vende de vuelta a los escribientes de la Compañía a tres cuartos. Todos saben exactamente lo que pasa.

finding_en: **The turned hook.** Look for a fishhook carved point-up, a hook that catches nothing, on a doorpost, under a tavern bench, or inked inside a ferryman's wrist. Then ask the keeper whether Aunt Brine is about.
**No business at a dawn fire.** The Keeping is sacred to thieves as much as to anyone.
**No paper.** Nothing written that a Holst clerk could read.
**A struck deal holds.** Borrowed from the Pocchin, and enforced harder.
**Nothing to the Inquisition.** The one line every crook in the islands agrees on.
**Don't drown the harbor.** No poaching pact-water, no breaking a port's sea-pact. The Quiet Auction keeps its own rules, which is why it is feared.
**Break one and you are cut loose:** no fence will touch your goods, no captain will carry you, no door with a turned hook will open.
finding_es: **El anzuelo volteado.** Busca un anzuelo tallado con la punta hacia arriba, un anzuelo que no pesca nada, en el marco de una puerta, debajo de un banco de taberna o tatuado en la muñeca de un barquero. Después pregúntale al dueño si anda por ahí la Tía Salmuera.
**Nada de negocios junto a un fuego del alba.** La [[Guarda|Keeping]] es sagrada para los ladrones tanto como para cualquiera.
**Nada de papel.** Nada escrito que pueda leer un escribiente de los Holst.
**Un trato cerrado se cumple.** Tomado de los pocchin, y se hace cumplir con más dureza.
**Nada a la Inquisición.** La única línea en la que están de acuerdo todos los maleantes de las islas.
**No ahogues el puerto.** Nada de pescar en aguas de pacto, nada de romper el pacto con el mar de un puerto. La Subasta Callada tiene sus propias reglas, y por eso le temen.
**Rompe una y te sueltan:** ningún reducidor toca tu mercancía, ningún capitán te lleva, ninguna puerta con un anzuelo volteado se abre.

black-coats: Nobody has ever bought a Black Coat and kept the receipt.
Nadie ha comprado nunca a una Casaca Negra y se ha quedado con el recibo.
pursuers: A Pursuer on your trail does not take coin.
Un Perseguidor tras tu rastro no acepta monedas.
chainbreakers: the Chainbreakers, who hunt slavers with no law at all
los Rompecadenas, que cazan esclavistas sin ley ninguna
The Chainbreakers do not take prisoners among slavers, and they do not take coin.
Los Rompecadenas no toman prisioneros entre los esclavistas, ni aceptan monedas.
whalers: The whalers do not sell the pact.
Los balleneros no venden el pacto.
hall: The fine is entered. Lords have paid it.
La multa se anota. Hasta los señores la han pagado.
chant: the chant-keepers, who send for you
los guardianes de los cantos, que te mandan llamar
Los guardianes de los cantos no aceptan monedas.

name: A town of the Frontier: the house-court
Un pueblo de la Frontera: el tribunal de la casa
court: the house-court, under Faust's iron law
el tribunal de la casa, bajo la ley de hierro de los Faust
wait_note: The house-court sits the morning after.
El tribunal de la casa sesiona a la mañana siguiente.
refused: The court takes it as an insult: ten lashes more.
El tribunal lo toma como un insulto: diez azotes más.
exile: exile from the house's lands; the sea does not forgive a man with nowhere to land
destierro de las tierras de la casa; el mar no perdona a quien no tiene dónde desembarcar
goes: To the house that holds the court; customs fines to House Holst, which keeps a tenth.
A la casa que preside el tribunal; las multas de aduana, a la Casa Holst, que se queda con una décima parte.
says: Harsh, swift, and martial. On the Frontier, mercy is a luxury and everyone knows the budget.
Dura, rápida y marcial. En la Frontera, la clemencia es un lujo y todos saben lo que cuesta.

name: Goldwind: the watch and the magistrates
Ventoro: la guardia y los magistrados
court: a magistrate of the city
un magistrado de la ciudad
wait_note: The magistrates sit on Sunsdawn, the day of law, when the docket reaches you.
Los magistrados sesionan en Albasol, el día de la ley, cuando les llega tu turno.
refused: The magistrate enters the offer in the record, and the sentence rises by half.
El magistrado anota la oferta en el expediente, y la pena sube a la mitad más.
exile: exile from the city, with your name at every gate
destierro de la ciudad, con tu nombre en cada puerta
goes: To the city's purse; customs fines to House Holst, which keeps a tenth.
A la bolsa de la ciudad; las multas de aduana, a la Casa Holst, que se queda con una décima parte.
says: Even-handed in principle and quietly weighted toward standing in practice. The Registry is enforced strictly within the walls.
Imparcial en principio y, en la práctica, inclinada en silencio hacia quien tiene posición. El Registro se aplica con rigor dentro de las murallas.

name: A lord's lands in the Heartland: the house-court
Las tierras de un señor en el Corazón: el tribunal de la casa
court: the lord's court, or the lord's steward
el tribunal del señor, o su mayordomo
wait_note: At the lord's next sitting.
En la próxima audiencia del señor.
refused: The steward remembers your face, and so does the lord.
El mayordomo recuerda tu cara, y el señor también.
exile: exile from the lord's lands
destierro de las tierras del señor
goes: To the lord, who sends a share up to the Council.
Al señor, que manda una parte al Consejo.
says: The Council's law, the Concord's moral weight, and the houses' own courts overlap. Wealth and standing bend outcomes, and everyone pretends otherwise.
La ley del Consejo, el peso moral de la Concordia y los tribunales de las casas se superponen. La riqueza y la posición tuercen los fallos, y todos fingen que no.

name: A Company town: the factor and the writ-men
Un pueblo de la Compañía: el factor y los hombres de escritos
court: the Company's factor, at a desk
el factor de la Compañía, detrás de un escritorio
wait_note: The factor's office, the same day.
La oficina del factor, el mismo día.
refused: The factor takes it anyway, and it goes on the paper.
El factor la acepta igual, y va al papel.
exile: turned out of the town, with the debt still on the paper
echado del pueblo, con la deuda todavía en el papel
goes: To the Company, on your paper.
A la Compañía, en tu papel.
says: A late bell, a broken tool, a word to an overseer: each is a fine, and each goes on the paper.
Una campana tarde, una herramienta rota, una palabra a un capataz: cada cosa es una multa, y cada multa va al papel.

name: A colonial port of the south: the Council's magistrate
Un puerto colonial del sur: el magistrado del Consejo
court: a colonial magistrate
un magistrado colonial
wait_note: When the magistrate is sober, or paid.
Cuando el magistrado está sobrio, o le pagaron.
refused: He keeps the money and the verdict both.
Se queda con el dinero y con el veredicto.
exile: exile from the colony
destierro de la colonia
goes: To the colonial purse, after the magistrate's share.
A la bolsa colonial, después de la parte del magistrado.
says: Colonial and Council law, too often corrupt. Which law reaches you depends entirely on who you are.
Ley colonial y del Consejo, demasiadas veces corrupta. Qué ley te alcanza depende por completo de quién eres.

name: Tribal lands of the south: the chant-keepers
Tierras de las tribus del sur: los guardianes de los cantos
court: the chant-keepers, at the council fire
los guardianes de los cantos, junto al fuego del consejo
wait_note: At the next council fire.
En el próximo fuego del consejo.
exile: sent from the tribe, and from the protection of its heart-fire
apartado de la tribu, y de la protección de su fuego del hogar
goes: To the one you wronged. The tribe keeps nothing.
A quien agraviaste. La tribu no se queda con nada.
says: Restorative judgment, which seeks to mend the tribe, and the war-codes for what cannot be mended.
Un juicio que repara, que busca sanar a la tribu, y los códigos de guerra para lo que no tiene arreglo.

name: A tyrant-house's lands in the south
Las tierras de una casa tirana del sur
court: the house's overseer, or its slaver-court
el capataz de la casa, o su tribunal esclavista
wait_note: Whenever the overseer has the time.
Cuando el capataz tenga tiempo.
refused: The overseer has you flogged for the presumption.
El capataz te hace azotar por el atrevimiento.
exile: driven out into the green
expulsado a la selva
goes: To the house.
A la casa.
says: The tyrant-houses' brutal order and the slaver-courts' legal fictions.
El orden brutal de las casas tiranas y las ficciones legales de los tribunales esclavistas.

name: A hold of the ice: the hold-lord's law
Una fortaleza del hielo: la ley del señor de la fortaleza
court: the hold-lord, in his hall
el señor de la fortaleza, en su salón
wait_note: At the hold-lord's next sitting.
En la próxima audiencia del señor de la fortaleza.
refused: The hold-lord keeps your coin for the hold, and adds the offer to the charge.
El señor de la fortaleza se queda tu moneda para la fortaleza, y suma la oferta al cargo.
exile: exile onto the ice, which in that cold is simply a slower sentence of death
destierro al hielo, que con ese frío es solo una sentencia de muerte más lenta
goes: To the hold.
A la fortaleza.
says: Sparse and hard. The ice forgives nothing.
Escasa y dura. El hielo no perdona nada.

name: Varan Port, Fairweather: coin and knife
Puerto Varan, Buentiempo: moneda y cuchillo
court: nobody; Mother Kess's people settle it
nadie; la gente de Madre Kess lo arregla
wait_note: Tonight.
Esta noche.
price_word: la gente de Kess se olvida del asunto
exile: put on the next ship out, whatever it is
subido al próximo barco que salga, sea cual sea
goes: To the one you wronged, and Kess's tenth on top.
A quien agraviaste, y encima el diezmo de Kess.
says: Coin, knife, and the corrupt Lodge. Kess's tenth is the only tax in Varan Port, and the only one never evaded.
Moneda, cuchillo y la Logia corrupta. El diezmo de Kess es el único impuesto de Puerto Varan, y el único que nadie evade.

name: The independent folk of the ice: blood-feud and exile
La gente libre del hielo: venganza de sangre y destierro
court: no court; the wronged family decides
ningún tribunal; decide la familia agraviada
wait_note: Whenever they find you.
Cuando te encuentren.
refused: The family takes the price as an insult to the dead.
La familia toma el precio como un insulto al muerto.
price_word: the family takes a blood-price instead
la familia acepta un precio de sangre a cambio
exile: exile from the hall, which on the ice is a slower death
destierro del salón, que en el hielo es una muerte más lenta
goes: To the family you wronged.
A la familia que agraviaste.
says: Among the independent folk, blood-feud and exile.
Entre la gente libre, venganza de sangre y destierro.

name: At sea: an Armada court
En altamar: un tribunal de la Armada
court: a court of Armada officers, in the next port with a flag
un tribunal de oficiales de la Armada, en el próximo puerto con insignia
wait_note: In the next port with a flag-officer; an Oathwarden keeps you until then.
En el próximo puerto con un oficial de insignia; hasta entonces te guarda un Guardajuramentos.
refused: Offering an officer coin is a second charge: six lashes more.
Ofrecerle dinero a un oficial es un segundo cargo: seis azotes más.
exile: put ashore on the nearest rock
desembarcado en la roca más cercana
goes: To the Armada's purse.
A la bolsa de la Armada.
says: The Oathwarden keeps the crew to Charter and oath. The Armada hangs pirates.
El Guardajuramentos mantiene a la tripulación fiel a la Carta y al juramento. La Armada ahorca piratas.

name: Below
Abajo
court: nobody; at law, Below is simply nowhere
nadie; ante la ley, Abajo no es ningún lugar
wait_note: No court sits Below.
Abajo no sesiona ningún tribunal.
says: The Charter stops at the rock. It is not illegal to go there. At law, it is simply nowhere.
La Carta se detiene en la roca. Ir allá no es ilegal. Ante la ley, simplemente no es ningún lugar.

name: A tavern brawl, fists only
Una pelea de taberna, solo a puñetazos
Drunk and loud in the street at night
Borracho y escandaloso en la calle de noche
A raised voice in the Quiet Room of the Reckoners' Hall
Alzar la voz en la Sala Silenciosa de la Casa de los Tesoreros
note: One Tide, entered against your name. A Gold Hunter once paid it, and asked for a receipt.
Una Marea, anotada contra tu nombre. Una vez la pagó una Cazadora de Oro, y pidió recibo.

name: Harming a lampet
Hacerle daño a un lapalumbre
note: The tavern beats you senseless first, and the magistrate hears the case with visible reluctance.
Primero la taberna te muele a golpes, y el magistrado oye el caso de muy mala gana.

name: Slipping out of harbor without paying the dues
Salir del puerto sin pagar los derechos
Turning a stranger out into the cold
Echar a un forastero al frío
none: No court here will hear it, and nobody who saw it will forget.
Ningún tribunal de aquí lo va a oír, y nadie que lo vio lo va a olvidar.

northern-frontier: The one unforgivable thing on the Frontier. The old fog-towns have hanged men for it.
Lo único imperdonable en la Frontera. Los viejos pueblos de niebla han ahorcado hombres por eso.
icy-expanse: On the ice, refusing food and fire to a traveler is murder, and is punished as murder.
En el hielo, negarle comida y fuego a un viajero es asesinato, y se castiga como asesinato.

name: Petty theft: a purse, a coat, a loaf
Un robo menor: una bolsa, un abrigo, un pan
Selling an unstamped chart as a true one
Vender una carta sin sello como si fuera buena
note: A chart is legal only with a Chartwrights' stamp.
Una carta solo es legal con el sello de los Cartógrafos.

name: Smuggling: goods landed without duty
Contrabando: mercancía desembarcada sin pagar derechos
note: The Grey Clerks have hanged more smugglers by ledger than the Armada ever has by cannon.
Los Escribanos Grises han ahorcado más contrabandistas con el libro de cuentas que la Armada con el cañón.

name: Casting without the copper rings
Lanzar conjuros sin los anillos de cobre
note: After the sentence you are enrolled, examined, and ringed. It is what makes the Ringless outlaws.
Después de la pena te inscriben, te examinan y te ponen los anillos. Es lo que hace de los Sin Anillo unos proscritos.

name: Assault with a blade, and nobody died
Una agresión con arma blanca, y nadie murió
Stealing a horse, a saurian, or a cargo
Robar un caballo, un saurio o una carga
A false customs seal, or a false manifest
Un sello de aduana falso, o un manifiesto falso
Casting at the Third Circle or above without a Writ
Lanzar un conjuro del Tercer Círculo o más sin un Mandato
note: The ring certifies; the Writ authorizes. The bell of it rings through every Krysta in the world.
El anillo certifica; el Mandato autoriza. Su campanada resuena en toda la Krysta del mundo.

name: Defiling a temple, or breaking a great oath
Profanar un templo, o romper un gran juramento
Wearing a brass Sigil (a false Hunter badge)
Llevar un Sello de latón (una insignia falsa de Cazador)
note: The Lodges hang the forger and badge-strip the buyer.
Las Logias ahorcan al falsificador y le quitan la insignia al comprador.

name: Deserting an Armada ship
Desertar de un barco de la Armada
Selling Sporrn poison
Vender veneno sporrn
note: Not sold on the surface, and hanged for.
En la superficie no se vende, y se ahorca por ella.

name: Forging a Chartwrights' stamp
Falsificar un sello de los Cartógrafos
Hanging a false light
Colgar una luz falsa
note: A hanging crime in every Council port.
Un crimen de horca en todos los puertos del Consejo.

name: Piracy
Piratería
note: A letter of marque makes it privateering, until the Navy decides it's awkward.
Una patente de corso lo vuelve corso, hasta que a la Armada le resulta incómodo.

name: Carrying ghost-cargo: captive people
Llevar carga fantasma: personas cautivas
note: Outlawed since the Great Slave Rebellion.
Prohibido desde la Gran Rebelión de los Esclavos.

tyrant: Here the slaver-courts call it indenture, and hear no case. The Chainbreakers hear it instead.
Aquí los tribunales esclavistas lo llaman servidumbre, y no oyen el caso. Lo oyen los Rompecadenas.

name: Forging Hunter Sigils
Falsificar Sellos de Cazador
note: The Lodges hang the forger.
Las Logias ahorcan al falsificador.

name: Harming a whale-wolf, or taking the tongue
Herir a un lobo ballenero, o quitarle la lengua

stations: Un forastero por quien nadie habla
A guild master or a merchant of standing
Un maestro de gremio o un mercader con posición

*: The Lodge's Quartermaster can pay a fine in chits, against your next contract.
El Intendente de la Logia puede pagar una multa con vales, a cuenta de tu próximo contrato.
fairweather: The Varan Lodge looks after its own, for a price.
La Logia de Varan cuida a los suyos, por un precio.
Mother Kess does not punish a noble. She ransoms one: a thousand Orsals to your house, and she takes a tenth for the courtesy.
Madre Kess no castiga a un noble. Lo rescata: mil Orsales a tu casa, y se queda con una décima parte por la cortesía.
tribal: The chant-keepers have no word for it.
Los guardianes de los cantos no tienen palabra para eso.

colonial: Which law reaches you depends entirely on who you are.
Qué ley te alcanza depende por completo de quién eres.

evidence: Atrapado con las manos en la masa
Por la palabra de un testigo

mines: {time} of labor in a Krysta mine
{time} de trabajo en una mina de Krysta
exile: {exile}
{exile}
bond: the fine goes on your paper: {coin}, worked off as a debt-bond
la multa va a tu papel: {coin}, que se paga trabajando como deuda
mend: restitution to the one you wronged: {coin}, or its worth
reparación a quien agraviaste: {coin}, o lo que valga
work: {time} of work for the household you wronged
{time} de trabajo para la casa que agraviaste
service: a year before the mast in an Armada hull, unpaid
un año al pie del mástil en un casco de la Armada, sin paga
feud: blood-feud: the wronged family may take it out of your hide, or your life
venganza de sangre: la familia agraviada puede cobrárselo con tu piel, o con tu vida
mark: Kess's people mark you, so the port remembers
la gente de Kess te marca, para que el puerto se acuerde
harbor: the harbor: you are not seen again
el puerto: no se te vuelve a ver
kess: pay the one you wronged {coin}, and Kess a tenth of it
pagarle {coin} a quien agraviaste, y a Kess una décima parte
sold: sold into indenture, which the slaver-court calls a debt
vendido como siervo, a lo que el tribunal esclavista llama deuda
beating: a beating, and then it is over
words: words at the council fire, and a gift to the one you wronged
palabras junto al fuego del consejo, y un regalo para quien agraviaste
nothing: nothing: nobody in Varan Port cares
nada: a nadie en Puerto Varan le importa

tribal: The chant-keepers do not keep the Council's ledgers. Here it is no wrong.
Los guardianes de los cantos no llevan los libros del Consejo. Aquí no es ningún agravio.
fairweather: In Varan Port the only tax is Kess's tenth, and the only crime is not paying it.
En Puerto Varan el único impuesto es el diezmo de Kess, y el único crimen es no pagarlo.
ice-free: Nobody out on the ice keeps the Council's law.
Allá afuera, en el hielo, nadie guarda la ley del Consejo.
below: The Charter stops at the rock.
La Carta se detiene en la roca.
No court sits Below. At law, it is simply nowhere.
Abajo no sesiona ningún tribunal. Ante la ley, simplemente no es ningún lugar.
The Knot keeps the peace by its own rules: no names, no blades, no light brighter than a candle.
El Nudo mantiene la paz con sus propias reglas: nada de nombres, nada de hojas, ninguna luz más fuerte que una vela.
Whoever you wronged settles it, if they can.
Quien sea que agraviaste lo arregla, si puede.
whalers: The one crime the whalers punish themselves. No hold-lord asks how.
El único crimen que los balleneros castigan ellos mismos. Ningún señor de fortaleza pregunta cómo.
kess: It has never been done. You would be the first, and the last.
Nunca se ha hecho. Serías el primero, y el último.

ledger: Three Coinsdays unpaid, and the debt goes to the Ledger. A name in the Ledger can borrow nowhere, sign no bottomry bond, and hold no master's chain in any guild.

Tres Monedías sin pagar, y la deuda pasa al Libro Mayor. Un nombre en el Libro Mayor no puede pedir prestado en ninguna parte, ni firmar un préstamo a la gruesa, ni llevar la cadena de maestro en ningún gremio.
bond: Debt-bond: you work it off, under a contract a magistrate seals. At a hand's wage, about {months}.
Deuda de trabajo: la pagas trabajando, con un contrato que sella un magistrado. Con sueldo de marinero, unos {months}.
hold: The debtors' hold: a long tide for those who cannot pay and will not bond. The debt keeps growing while they sit.
La cárcel de deudores: una marea larga para quien no puede pagar y no quiere firmar. La deuda sigue creciendo mientras esperan.
company: In a Company town it is indenture, and the debt somehow never shrinks.
En un pueblo de la Compañía es servidumbre, y la deuda, no se sabe cómo, nunca se achica.
still: The Still Days freeze every debt in the islands: no interest runs, no debt is called, and no debtor may be taken.
Los Días Quietos congelan toda deuda de las islas: no corre interés, no se cobra ninguna deuda, y a ningún deudor se lo pueden llevar.
wolves: Varan Port has no Ledger. It has the Ledger Wolves: one in ten every Cycle, collected by knife.
Puerto Varan no tiene Libro Mayor. Tiene a los Lobos del Libro Mayor: uno de cada diez cada Ciclo, cobrado a cuchillo.
none: No ledger reaches here. What you owe, you owe to a face.
Ningún libro de cuentas llega hasta aquí. Lo que debes, se lo debes a una cara.

still: The courts close for the Still Days. The trial waits until the year turns.
Los tribunales cierran en los Días Quietos. El juicio espera a que cambie el año.

rules: Nine ports lie in a ring on the board. At each one a tile is turned: the cargo that port is buying, and how many marks it pays a tile.
Nueve puertos forman un anillo en el tablero. En cada uno se voltea una ficha: la carga que ese puerto compra, y cuántas marcas paga por ficha.
Every captain holds five tiles, face down: six cargoes, and a few rocks that sell for nothing.
Cada capitán tiene cinco fichas boca abajo: seis cargas, y unas cuantas piedras que no valen nada.
In turn, each captain may land one to three tiles and swear they are what the port is buying. It may be true.
Por turno, cada capitán puede desembarcar de una a tres fichas y jurar que son lo que el puerto compra. Puede ser verdad.

Anyone may call “Open the hold!” If the tiles are true, the port pays for them, and the caller pays the captain a mark a tile besides. If one is false, the captain pays the caller a mark a tile and sells nothing.

Cualquiera puede gritar “¡Abre la bodega!”. Si las fichas son verdad, el puerto las paga, y además quien gritó le paga al capitán una marca por ficha. Si alguna es falsa, el capitán le paga a quien gritó una marca por ficha y no vende nada.
With a Gaming Set (Nine Ports tiles), a captain's tells mean something three times in four.
Con un juego de Nueve Puertos, los gestos de un capitán significan algo tres veces de cada cuatro.
If nobody calls, the port pays for every tile, true or not. Then everyone draws back up to five.
Si nadie grita, el puerto paga cada ficha, sea verdad o no. Después todos vuelven a robar hasta tener cinco.
After the ninth port, the richest captain takes the pot.
Después del noveno puerto, el capitán más rico se lleva el bote.
styles: plays the odds and nothing else
juega a las probabilidades y a nada más
lies for the pleasure of it
miente por el gusto de mentir
cheats as a matter of courtesy, and says so
hace trampa por cortesía, y lo dice

lie: touches the rim of a cup that is not there
toca el borde de una taza que no está
lands the tiles a little too gently
baja las fichas con demasiada delicadeza
names the cargo before the port is read
nombra la carga antes de que se lea el puerto
looks at your hands, not the tiles
te mira las manos, no las fichas
se ríe medio suspiro antes de tiempo
true: lands the tiles and forgets them
desembarca las fichas y se olvida de ellas
pushes the tiles at you, daring you

pocchin: draws a sixth tile, as a courtesy, and tells the whole table.
roba una sexta ficha, por cortesía, y se lo dice a toda la mesa.
swaps a tile with the bag, as a courtesy, and apologizes beautifully.
cambia una ficha con la bolsa, por cortesía, y se disculpa con mucha elegancia.

name: Gatehold
Fortín de la Puerta
what: A board game where one player holds a gate with few pieces against many. Faust officers train on it, and children play it on chalked doorsteps.
Un juego de tablero en el que un jugador defiende una puerta con pocas piezas contra muchas. Los oficiales de los Faust entrenan con él, y los niños lo juegan en escalones pintados con tiza.
check: Inteligencia, con un juego de Fortín de la Puerta
beats: The gate holds a round longer than it should.
La puerta aguanta una ronda más de lo que debería.
A feint on the left, and the real push comes through the middle.
Un amago por la izquierda, y el empuje de verdad llega por el centro.
Three pieces lost to take one tower.
Tres piezas perdidas para tomar una torre.
The defender gives up the yard to keep the keep.
El defensor cede el patio para conservar la torre del homenaje.

name: Council
Consejo
what: A card game of five seats and shifting alliances, banned twice by the real Council for being “uncomfortably accurate.”
Un juego de cartas de cinco asientos y alianzas cambiantes, prohibido dos veces por el Consejo de verdad por ser “incómodamente preciso”.
beats: An alliance is sworn, and broken before the next hand.
Se jura una alianza, y se rompe antes de la siguiente mano.
The Admiralty's seat votes with the Hunters, and nobody saw it coming.
El asiento del Almirantazgo vota con los Cazadores, y nadie lo vio venir.
A bribe card changes hands under the table.
Una carta de soborno cambia de manos por debajo de la mesa.
Somebody laughs: it is exactly what happened last session.
Alguien se ríe: es exactamente lo que pasó en la última sesión.

name: The sowing board
El tablero de siembra
what: Seeds sown round a carved board of pits. Every village square has one, and the old men are unbeatable.
Semillas sembradas alrededor de un tablero tallado con hoyos. Cada plaza de pueblo tiene uno, y los viejos son imbatibles.
beats: A long sowing lands the last seed in an empty pit, and takes the row.
Una siembra larga deja la última semilla en un hoyo vacío, y se lleva la fila.
The old man does not look at the board. He looks at you.
El viejo no mira el tablero. Te mira a ti.
Four pits empty in a single sowing.
Cuatro hoyos se vacían en una sola siembra.
A child watching whispers the right move, too late.
Un niño que mira susurra la jugada buena, demasiado tarde.

name: Bone-dice
Dados de hueso
what: The ice's dice, carved from whalebone, thrown on a sealskin by the lamp.
Los dados del hielo, tallados en hueso de ballena, que se tiran sobre una piel de foca junto a la lámpara.
check: no check: three dice each, the highest wins
ninguna prueba: tres dados cada uno, gana el más alto
beats: The dice turn over once more on the sealskin, and stop.
Los dados dan una vuelta más sobre la piel de foca, y se detienen.
Somebody blows on the bones for luck. It does not help.
Alguien sopla los huesos para tener suerte. No sirve.
A die rolls off into the dark and has to be found.
Un dado rueda hacia la oscuridad y hay que buscarlo.
The lamp gutters, and every hand covers its dice.
La lámpara titubea, y cada mano tapa sus dados.

name: The Long Tell
El Cuento Largo
where: the ice, in the Long Night
el hielo, en la Larga Noche
what: A winter contest to tell one story the longest without repeating a single tale. It keeps a hall sane through the Long Night.
Un concurso de invierno: contar una sola historia el mayor tiempo posible sin repetir ningún relato. Mantiene cuerdo un salón durante la Larga Noche.
beats: The story goes down a whale-road and comes back with a new captain.
La historia baja por un camino de ballenas y vuelve con un capitán nuevo.
The hall laughs at the right place, and the lamp is trimmed.
El salón se ríe en el lugar justo, y se despabila la lámpara.
An old woman says “I've heard that one,” and is shushed.
Una anciana dice “esa ya la oí”, y la hacen callar.
The tale borrows a ghost from the Grey Fathoms, and gives it back.
El relato le pide prestado un fantasma a las Brazas Grises, y se lo devuelve.

name: The Haul
El Arrastre
what: Crew against crew, rope-hauling on the docks, pulled to a shanty's beat. It settles disputes between crews.
Tripulación contra tripulación, tirando de una cuerda en los muelles al compás de una saloma. Arregla las disputas entre tripulaciones.
beats: The shanty drops a beat, and the rope goes three feet the wrong way.
La saloma pierde un compás, y la cuerda se va un metro para el otro lado.
Somebody's boots find a wet plank.
Las botas de alguien encuentran una tabla mojada.
The anchor of the line sits down and will not move.
El último de la cuerda se sienta y no hay quien lo mueva.
The whole quay sings the last verse.
Todo el muelle canta la última estrofa.

name: Tidecall
Llamada de la Marea
what: Seven against seven at low water, a floating cork ball called the buoy, two posts called the marks, and no clock: it ends when the tide reaches the callstone.
Siete contra siete con la marea baja, una pelota de corcho que flota llamada la boya, dos postes llamados las marcas, y ningún reloj: termina cuando la marea llega a la piedra de la llamada.
check: Dexterity (Athletics or Acrobatics), the side together
Destreza (Atletismo o Acrobacias), todo el equipo
beats: The buoy skims off a wave and through the marks.
La boya rebota en una ola y pasa entre las marcas.
Knee-deep now: last water.
Ya hasta las rodillas: última agua.
A sailor goes under and comes up with the buoy.
Un marinero se hunde y sale con la boya.
The tide calls it.
La marea decide.

name: The Long Throw
El Lanzamiento Largo
what: Harpoon-throwing for distance and aim at a floating mark.
Lanzamiento de arpón, de distancia y puntería, a una marca que flota.
check: Dexterity or Strength, a harpoon (an attack roll)
Destreza o Fuerza, un arpón (una tirada de ataque)
beats: The harpoon hums out over the water and stands in the mark.
El arpón zumba sobre el agua y se clava en la marca.
The wind takes it a hand's breadth wide.
El viento lo desvía un palmo.
The whalers stamp on the ice for a good throw.
Los balleneros zapatean en el hielo por un buen lanzamiento.
The mark is hit so hard it sinks.
Le pegan a la marca tan fuerte que se hunde.

name: The Hold
El Agarre
what: Wrestling on ice: the first to touch down loses.
Lucha sobre el hielo: el primero que toca el suelo pierde.
beats: Both slide a yard, locked, and neither falls.
Los dos resbalan un metro, trabados, y ninguno cae.
A knee almost touches. Almost.
Una rodilla casi toca. Casi.
The crowd counts the breaths.
La gente cuenta las respiraciones.
One foot finds the rough ice, and that is the end of it.
Un pie encuentra el hielo áspero, y ahí se acaba.

name: Ringstone (ukkora)
Anillo de piedra (ukkora)
what: A heavy sap-rubber ball struck only with hip, thigh, and forearm through a stone ring set high on a court wall, played at festivals and to settle quarrels between villages under a chant-keeper's eye.

Una pesada pelota de caucho que solo se golpea con la cadera, el muslo y el antebrazo, a través de un anillo de piedra puesto en lo alto de la pared de una cancha; se juega en las fiestas y para arreglar pleitos entre pueblos, bajo la mirada de un guardián de los cantos.
beats: The ball kisses the ring and falls back.
La pelota besa el anillo y cae de vuelta.
A hip-strike from the floor, and the whole court gasps.
Un golpe de cadera desde el suelo, y toda la cancha contiene el aliento.
The chant-keeper raises a hand: a forearm too many.
El guardián de los cantos levanta la mano: un antebrazo de más.
Through the ring.
A través del anillo.

name: The Pick
La Rebusca
what: A goblin contest to find the most valuable thing in a junk-heap in the time it takes a candle-notch to burn.
Un concurso goblin: encontrar lo más valioso de un montón de chatarra en lo que tarda en quemarse una marca de la vela.
beats: A spoon, a buckle, a key to nothing.
Una cuchara, una hebilla, una llave de nada.
Something under the heap is ticking.
Algo debajo del montón hace tic tac.
A real Tide, green with age.
Una Marea de verdad, verde de vieja.
The candle reaches the notch.
La vela llega a la marca.

name: A stillness-contest
Un concurso de quietud
where: los estanques de peces de los hombres lagarto
what: Who can stand motionless longest beside the fish-pool.
Quién se queda inmóvil más tiempo junto al estanque.
beats: A fly lands on an eyelid.
Una mosca se posa en un párpado.
The sun moves a finger's width.
El sol se mueve un dedo.
A fish rises. Nobody looks.
Sube un pez. Nadie mira.
Somebody's tail twitches, and everyone pretends not to see it.
A alguien se le mueve la cola, y todos fingen no verlo.

name: Title-bellowing
Bramar títulos
where: donde se juntan las caravanas pocchin
what: A Pocchin contest of roaring out one's titles, longest and loudest.
Un concurso pocchin: rugir los propios títulos, lo más largo y lo más fuerte posible.
beats: A title is invented on the spot, and the crowd allows it.
Se inventa un título en el momento, y la gente lo acepta.
The grommoths bellow back.
Los grommoths braman en respuesta.
Somebody runs out of breath on “and Keeper of the Third Sand-Tub.”
A alguien se le acaba el aire en “y Guardián de la Tercera Tina de Arena”.
The caravan-mother nods once.
La madre de la caravana asiente una vez.

name: A kite-duel
Un duelo de cometas
where: la Colina de las Cometas de Ventoro
what: Fighting kites on lines glassed to cut. Two kites cross lines, and the first line cut loses.
Cometas de pelea con hilos cubiertos de vidrio para cortar. Dos cometas cruzan los hilos, y pierde el primer hilo cortado.
check: Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), with the line
Destreza (Juego de Manos), con el hilo
beats: The lines cross and saw, and the harbor wall roars.
Los hilos se cruzan y se sierran, y el muro del puerto ruge.
A dive under the other kite, and up.
Una picada por debajo de la otra cometa, y arriba.
The wind drops for a breath. Both kites fall a yard.
El viento cae por un instante. Las dos cometas bajan un metro.
A cut kite, and every runner on the hill is already running.
Una cometa cortada, y todos los corredores de la colina ya van corriendo.

opponents: An old man of the village square (the sowing board)
Un viejo de la plaza del pueblo (el tablero de siembra)

name: Swiftcrest racing at the Sunspine Run
Carreras de crestaveloz en la Carrera del Espinazo del Sol
what: Champion bloodlines, daredevil jockeys, and fortunes in wagers. The reigning champion, the silver-crested Sissix-the-Comet, has not lost a heat in two seasons.
Linajes campeones, jinetes temerarios y fortunas en apuestas. El campeón reinante, Sissix-el-Cometa, de cresta plateada, no ha perdido una manga en dos temporadas.

name: A gig race: the Long Pull
Una regata de botes: el Tirón Largo
where: every harbor; the crown at Goldwind's Festival of Winds
todos los puertos; la corona en la Fiesta de los Vientos de Ventoro
what: Six- and eight-oared boats rowed flat-out across a harbor course. Crew loyalty is lifelong and the crew songs get ruder each year.
Botes de seis y ocho remos a toda fuerza por un recorrido de puerto. La lealtad a la tripulación dura toda la vida y las canciones de cada tripulación son más groseras cada año.

name: The Peg Leg Race
La Carrera de la Pata de Palo
where: at sea, once a day on a long voyage
en altamar, una vez al día en un viaje largo
what: Every hand who wants to runs a lap of the deck with one leg tied up, and the cook keeps the book.
Cada marinero que quiere da una vuelta a la cubierta con una pierna atada, y el cocinero lleva las apuestas.

name: A fight on Kitehill
Una pelea en la Colina de las Cometas
what: Every fight has odds, and the kite-gamblers chalk them on the Chalk Wall, and wipe them off when the watch comes up the hill.
Cada pelea tiene probabilidades, y los apostadores de cometas las anotan con tiza en el Muro de Tiza, y las borran cuando la guardia sube la colina.

unbeaten: Sable Wren, the Unbeaten, of the Red Spool
Sable Wren, la Invicta, del Carrete Rojo
fix: Buy the fix from the Crest Syndicate: a fifth of the winnings, and a favor owed to the Odds-Mother
Comprar el arreglo al Sindicato de la Cresta: una quinta parte de la ganancia, y un favor que se le debe a la Madre de las Apuestas
